content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe the three states of matter and their properties
Explain the arrangement and movement of particles in each state
Use the particle model to explain properties of solids, liquids, and gases
Explain the limitations of the particle model
Matter exists in three main states:
. The properties of each state can be explained by the arrangement, movement, and energy of the particles that make up the substance.
Particles are closely packed in a regular arrangement
Strong forces between particles hold them in place
[DIAGRAM: Particle arrangement in solid - regular pattern]
Particles are close together but not in a regular arrangement
Particles can move around each other
Forces between particles are weaker than in solids
[DIAGRAM: Particle arrangement in liquid - irregular, touching]
Particles are far apart with no regular arrangement
Particles move quickly in all directions
[DIAGRAM: Particle arrangement in gas - widely spaced, moving randomly]
Explaining Properties Using the Particle Model
Why do solids have a fixed shape?
Particles are held in fixed positions by strong forces
They can only vibrate, not move to new positions
Particles can move around each other
They are not held in fixed positions
The liquid can change shape to fit its container
Particles are far apart with lots of empty space
When pressure is applied, particles move closer together
There is little empty space between them
Why are gases less dense than liquids and solids?
There are fewer particles in the same volume
Less mass per unit volume = lower density
Ice is unusual - it's less dense than liquid water (which is why ice floats).
is the spreading out of particles from an area of high concentration to an area of low concentration.
Diffusion happens because particles are constantly moving randomly.
Diffusion is fastest in gases because:
There is more space between particles
Fewer collisions to slow particles down
Diffusion is slowest in solids because:
Particles can only vibrate in fixed positions
They cannot move to new positions
The simple particle model has some limitations:
Particles are shown as solid spheres
- in reality, atoms have internal structure
Forces between particles are not shown
- the model doesn't show the attractions
- doesn't show different types of atoms or molecules
- can't see kinetic energy of particles
Despite these limitations, the particle model is very useful for explaining properties of matter.
is the random movement of small particles suspended in a fluid (liquid or gas), caused by collisions with particles of the fluid.
Smoke particles in air move randomly because air molecules collide with them.
Gas particles move faster than liquid particles
Saying particles get bigger when heated
Particles move faster and spread out, but don't change size
The spaces between particles are empty (vacuum)
Saying particles in a solid don't move
Particles vibrate about fixed positions; they don't move to new positions
Describe the arrangement of particles in a solid. (2 marks)
Explain why liquids can flow but solids cannot. (3 marks)
Explain why gases can be compressed but liquids cannot. (3 marks)
Use the particle model to explain why a gas has a lower density than a liquid. (3 marks)
A drop of ink is placed in water. After a few hours, the ink has spread throughout the water. Explain this observation using the particle model. (3 marks)
State two limitations of the particle model. (2 marks)
A state of matter with fixed shape and volume
A state of matter with fixed volume but no fixed shape
A state of matter with no fixed shape or volume
A model that explains the behaviour of matter using particles
The spreading of particles from high to low concentration
Random movement of particles caused by collisions with fluid particles
particles vibrate in fixed positions, fixed shape and volume
particles move around each other, fixed volume but not shape
particles move randomly and fast, no fixed shape or volume
Properties can be explained by particle arrangement and movement
is fastest in gases, slowest in solids
The particle model has limitations but is useful for explaining properties
